transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Could you tell me what brings you in today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you so much for fitting me in. Um... I hope I'm not wasting your time, but I came in because I've been acting a little... well, out of character lately. 

I've started doing some things that honestly kind of scare me. I hope that doesn't sound too dramatic, I just... well, for example, I'll just walk out in the middle of major software deployments at work, which is incredibly unprofessional and so unlike me. Or I'll just get in my car and drive around late at night with no plan or destination at all. 

I'm usually a very responsible, organized person, I promise. It's just... that is not how I've ever handled stress before, and I don't want to mess up my career or my life. Does that make sense? I just wanted to make sure I was doing the right thing by coming to see you about it.
Have you been feeling unusually energized, elevated, or irritable lately?

Oh, um... no, I don't think so. Definitely not energized or, you know, elevated. If anything, I'm just a bit drained most days. And I really try my best not to be irritable with anyone, especially my coworkers. I hope I don't come across as irritable to you right now! 

I just... no, I haven't noticed any sudden bursts of energy or anything like that. Is that alright? I just want to make sure I'm answering your questions properly and giving you the right information.
Have you noticed a decrease in your interest or enjoyment in activities that you used to find pleasurable, like hobbies, work, or time with friends and family?

Well, um... I guess maybe a little bit? I hope it doesn't make me sound like a bad friend or anything, but I have been staying in more than usual. 

I used to be really active—I'd plan my whole week around salsa dancing, my book club, yoga classes, or having people over to cook Guatemalan food. I always loved hosting and making sure everyone had a good time. But lately... I don't know, I just haven't had it in me. I've been canceling a lot, which I feel terrible about. I just end up sitting at home, scrolling on my phone or putting a show on but not really watching it. 

I know I need to get back out there, I promise I'm trying. Is it normal to just need a break from socializing sometimes? I hope I'm not making too big a deal out of it.
Have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most days, even when there’s no obvious reason for it?

Um... well, no, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad or hopeless. I mean, I definitely don't want to sound like I'm complaining or feeling sorry for myself, you know? 

I guess I've just been feeling a little... flat? Or maybe just tired. But definitely not hopeless. I know I have a lot to be grateful for—a good job, great friends, a nice home. I really try to focus on the positive things. I hope that makes sense? I just don't want you to think I'm ungrateful or depressed or anything like that. I'm just in a bit of a slump, I think. Is that an okay answer?
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight lately, like eating much more or much less than usual?

Um... no, I don't think so. My appetite has been pretty normal, I'd say. I mean, I always try to make sure I'm eating enough and taking care of myself. 

I definitely haven't gained or lost any noticeable weight. I mean, maybe a pound or two here and there, but nothing major, you know? I try really hard to maintain a healthy diet. I hope that's what you were looking for? I just want to make sure I'm giving you all the right details.
Have you noticed any changes in your sleep lately, like sleeping much more or much less than usual, or trouble falling or staying asleep?

Well, um... I guess sleep has been a little tricky lately? I really don't want to sound like I'm whining, because I know everyone has trouble sleeping sometimes, right? 

But, um... most nights, I just sort of lie there. My brain just keeps replaying pieces of... well, of the incident at the office. I try so hard to just turn it off and think about pleasant things, I promise I do. But then when I finally do manage to drift off, I end up waking up feeling all tense. Sometimes it's from a bad dream, or even just some tiny little noise in the house. 

So I guess I've been pretty exhausted before work even starts. I hope I'm not making it sound worse than it is. Is it normal to have your mind race like that when you're just trying to get some rest? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Have you had experiences like this before, where you felt off or out of sorts, or is this the first time you've noticed these kinds of changes in yourself?

Um... well, no, I wouldn't say I've ever felt quite like this before. I mean, I've always been a pretty steady person, you know? I usually handle stress really well, and I don't want you to think I'm someone who just falls apart over every little thing. 

But, um... this specific feeling, the trouble sleeping and everything... it's been happening since that late-night cutover incident at the office. I guess that was a little over a year ago now? Maybe about 13 months? 

I really kept thinking I would just bounce back, because that's what I usually do. I didn't want to make a big fuss about it. I hope it's okay that I waited this long to talk to someone? I just kept hoping I could push through it on my own and not bother anyone with it. Does that make sense?

Have you ever had a period where you felt unusually high, extremely confident, or unusually irritable for several days or more — maybe even feeling like you didn't need much sleep or that your thoughts were racing?

Um... no, definitely not. I've never felt anything like that. I mean, I'm a pretty even-keeled person, usually. I don't really get those kind of extreme highs or act overly confident or anything. I try to just stay grounded and focus on doing a good job at work, you know?

And I definitely haven't felt like I didn't need sleep. Like I said, I really want to sleep, I just... struggle with it right now. I don't want you to think I'm acting erratic or anything like that. I'm just a normal person having a hard time. I hope that's the right answer? I just want to be sure I'm giving you the clear picture.

Can you tell me a bit more about the late-night cutover incident at the office that you mentioned earlier? Did something specific happen during that night that was particularly stressful or upsetting for you?

Um... gosh. I know I brought it up, so I should probably explain it. But, um... is it alright if we don't get into the exact details right now? 

I just... I feel so silly even talking about it. I really don't want to sound like I'm blowing things out of proportion, because I know people go through much worse things, right? It was just... a really, really bad situation while I was working late. 

I'm sorry, I know I'm probably being difficult and that's not a very helpful answer. I just get so worked up trying to explain it, and I really don't want you to think I'm just being dramatic or oversensitive. I promise I'll tell you, I just... is it okay if we maybe talk about that part a little later? I hope you're not frustrated with me for holding back.
Can you describe what happened during the late-night cutover incident? Did something occur that felt threatening, overwhelming, or traumatic to you at the time?

Um... I know you just asked about that, and I'm really sorry to be so difficult. I don't mean to be dodging the question, I really don't. 

It's just... well, it was overwhelming, yes. But I don't know if I'd call it "traumatic," because that sounds like such a strong word, you know? Like I'm claiming to be a victim of something huge when I'm just a systems analyst who was working a late shift. I really don't want to come across like I'm making a mountain out of a molehill. 

I just... I'm not quite ready to walk through the specifics of what happened that night. It just makes my chest feel really tight when I try to picture it, and I want to be a good patient and give you all the information, but... could we please just skip the details for today? I hope that's okay. I'm really trying my best here, I promise.
Have you noticed yourself feeling unusually anxious, especially when reminded of the cutover incident or when thinking about going through something similar again?

Um... yes, I guess I have been feeling pretty anxious. But it's not just when I think about that night, honestly. 

It's kind of... well, even on the quiet days, when everything at work is fine and I'm just sitting at my desk, I still have this... this heavy mix of fear and, I don't know, shame, just sitting right here in my chest. Like I should have handled everything so much better than I did, you know? And I just can't shake this feeling that something bad could still happen if I let my guard down for even a second. 

I know that probably sounds so silly, feeling ashamed over a work thing. I really hope I'm not coming across as totally irrational. I'm just trying to be honest about how I've been feeling... is that the kind of thing you were asking about?
Have you found yourself avoiding certain people, places, or thoughts because they remind you of what happened during that late-night cutover incident?

Um... yes, I suppose I have been doing that a little bit. I really hope it doesn't make me sound like I'm not a team player, because I still get all my work done, I promise! 

But, um... I do kind of find myself taking the long way around the building now. Just to... well, to avoid that specific floor whenever I can. It's just easier that way, so I don't get worked up over nothing. And, um, if people at work start talking about the contractor, or... or the cutover, I just sort of shut the conversation down right away. Or I make an excuse to go back to my desk. 

I know that's probably not very polite of me, and I hate being rude to my coworkers. I really do. Does that make sense? I hope I'm answering your question okay... I just don't want you to think I'm slacking off at my job or anything.
